headline: DNS resolves fine, TCP 80 is open, but the HTTP response stalls because of a path-MTU black hole: only packets up to 1000 bytes cross the path, larger ones are dropped, and the ICMP 'fragmentation needed' message that should tell the sender to shrink them never arrives.

findings.message: Path-MTU black hole: packets larger than 1000 bytes are silently dropped. Small exchanges (ping, TCP handshake, the request) work; the large HTTP response packets do not.
findings.evidence: DF ping of 972 bytes payload passes, one byte more is lost with no ICMP error
findings.remedy: Stop filtering ICMP type 3 code 4 on the path. Until then, clamp TCP MSS on the router (iptables -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu) or lower the interface MTU on the endpoints.

checks.title: Path MTU (DF-bit ping sweep)
checks.summary: Packets up to 1000 bytes get through, but anything larger with Don't-Fragment set vanishes without an ICMP 'fragmentation needed' reply. That is the signature of a path-MTU black hole.
